speaker: Sheldon
text: Yes. In fact, he was quite enthusiastic. He said, frankly, if I could send you tonight, I would. Of course not. I'm a theoretical physicist, a career I chose in no small part because it's indoors. But if I'm able to detect slow-moving magnetic monopoles there, I will be the scientist to confirm string theory. People will write books about me. Third graders will create macaroni art dioramas depicting scenes from my life.

speaker: Leonard
text: He offered to send you to the North Pole? Hey, well, do I know?

speaker: Leonard
text: Sure. Maybe a tableau of me trying to pummel you to death.

speaker: Sheldon
text: I'm on the horns of a dilemma. Can you imagine me, Sheldon Cooper, at the North Pole?

speaker: Leonard
text: Easy peasy. I'm doing it right now.

speaker: Sheldon
text: I'm not good with cold, Leonard. How often have we had to leave a movie theater because I got a headache from drinking the icy too fast? I can't go.

speaker: Sheldon
text: How can you say that? A scientific opportunity of a lifetime presents itself and my best friend says don't go.
